sections.description: This section outlines the patient’s history, symptom onset, and the first clinical and laboratory assessments that prompted further investigation.
subtopics: Patient demographics and past medical history (obesity, NAFLD, hypertension, hypothyroidism, prior DVT/PE)
Timeline of semaglutide exposure and acute gastrointestinal reaction
Early hospital course: volume depletion, acute renal failure, metabolic acidosis, modest CK elevation
Progressive neuromuscular symptoms over four months (proximal weakness, dysphagia, dysphonia)
Physical examination findings on tertiary referral (proximal muscle strength, absence of rash or other systemic signs)
Initial laboratory panel: CK trend, liver enzymes, thyroid function, basic metabolic panel

sections.description: This section walks through the systematic consideration of possible causes of the myopathy and the targeted investigations that narrowed the diagnosis to immune‑mediated necrotising myopathy (IMNM).
subtopics: Broad differential for acute and sub‑acute proximal muscle weakness (toxic rhabdomyolysis, inflammatory myopathies, metabolic myopathies, endocrine, neuromuscular junction, structural myopathies)
Key features arguing against pure rhabdomyolysis (CK trajectory, lack of myoglobinuria, delayed CK peak)
Rationale for auto‑immune myopathy work‑up despite negative ANA and myositis panel
Serologic testing: myositis‑specific antibodies (HMGCR, SRP, Jo‑1, etc.) and interpretation of seronegative IMNM
Imaging studies: MRI of thigh showing muscle edema, cardiac MRI and echocardiography to assess for myocarditis/ stress cardiomyopathy
Muscle biopsy findings: necrotic/regenerating fibers, macrophage infiltrates (CD68), membrane attack complex deposition, sparse CD3+ T‑cells – diagnostic criteria for IMNM
Exclusion of alternative organ involvement (liver biopsy, CT chest, pulmonary evaluation) and assessment of cardiac biomarkers

sections.section_title: Pathophysiology of Immune‑Mediated Necrotising Myopathy and the Role of GLP‑1 Receptor Agonists
sections.description: This section provides the mechanistic background of IMNM, the known drug‑induced variants, and explores how semaglutide could act as a trigger.
subtopics: Definition of IMNM: clinical phenotype, histologic hallmarks, and serologic subsets (HMGCR, SRP, seronegative)
Immune mechanisms: complement activation (MAC deposition), macrophage‑mediated myophagocytosis, limited T‑cell infiltrate
Established drug‑associated IMNM (statins → HMGCR antibodies) – parallels and differences
GLP‑1 receptor agonist pharmacology: metabolic effects, GI side‑effects, reported muscle‑mass changes
Potential immunologic pathways linking GLP‑1 agonism to autoimmunity (altered cytokine milieu, molecular mimicry, off‑target immune activation)
Evidence from case reports of tirzepatide‑related rhabdomyolysis and how the current case diverges (CK magnitude, time course, need for immunosuppression)
Application of WHO‑UMC causality criteria to this case (temporal relationship, de‑challenge, lack of rechallenge, alternative causes ruled out)

sections.description: This section details the stepwise immunosuppressive regimen, supportive care measures, and the patient’s recovery trajectory.
subtopics: Initial high‑dose intravenous methylprednisolone pulse and rationale
Transition to oral prednisone (dose, tapering schedule) and monitoring for side‑effects
Use of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG): dosing, indications for IVIG in IMNM, expected benefits
Supportive measures during acute phase (hydration, renal monitoring, cardiac surveillance)
Complications encountered (septic shock from pseudomonal UTI) and impact on management
Outcome metrics: CK normalization timeline, functional recovery (strength, dysphagia resolution), cardiac imaging normalization
Long‑term follow‑up: withdrawal of immunosuppression, avoidance of GLP‑1 agonists, durability of remission

sections.section_title: Clinical Implications, Pharmacovigilance, and Future Directions
sections.description: This final section synthesizes the lessons learned, proposes practice points for clinicians, and outlines research needs regarding GLP‑1 agonist‑related myopathy.
subtopics: Recognition of atypical drug‑induced myopathy versus classic rhabdomyolysis in patients on GLP‑1 agonists
Algorithm for evaluating new‑onset muscle weakness in patients receiving semaglutide or related agents
Importance of early muscle biopsy when serology is negative and CK remains markedly elevated
Guidance on discontinuation of the offending agent and brief immunosuppression versus prolonged therapy
Reporting adverse events to pharmacovigilance databases (FAERS, WHO‑VigiBase) to capture rare IMNM cases
Potential risk factors to investigate (pre‑existing liver disease, autoantibody profile, genetic predisposition)
Research agenda: prospective surveillance, mechanistic studies of GLP‑1‑related immune activation, and registry development
